events.title: Henry IV of France Converts to Catholicism
events.description: After years of religious civil war, the Protestant-raised king publicly renounced his faith and embraced Roman Catholicism in a ceremony at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
events.significance: The move helped end France's Wars of Religion and secured Henry's acceptance as king. It paved the way for the Edict of Nantes in 1598, which granted religious toleration to French Protestants.

events.title: James I Crowned King of England and Scotland
events.description: James VI of Scotland was crowned at Westminster Abbey as James I of England, ruling both kingdoms after the death of Elizabeth I.
events.significance: The Union of the Crowns brought the two realms under one monarch for the first time, a step toward the eventual creation of Great Britain.

events.title: Blériot Flies Across the English Channel
events.description: French aviator Louis Blériot piloted his Blériot XI monoplane from France to England in about 36 minutes, becoming the first person to cross the Channel by airplane.
events.significance: The flight showed that aircraft could cross natural barriers that had long protected nations. It sparked huge public excitement about aviation and its military potential.

events.title: Tunisia Becomes a Republic
events.description: A year after gaining independence from France, Tunisia abolished its monarchy and proclaimed a republic, with Habib Bourguiba as its first president.
events.significance: Bourguiba's long leadership shaped modern Tunisia, which pursued notable social reforms, including expanded women's rights, in the post-colonial Arab world.
